bull.b: First-ever positive adjusted EBITDA, achieved ahead of plan, shows that cost reductions and operating discipline are beginning to translate into improved earnings quality. If maintained, this milestone could support self-funded growth and make the charging platform more resilient over the next several quarters.

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 55%, while repeat and recurring revenue accounted for about 55% of total revenue. A richer revenue mix and higher-margin contracts can improve earnings durability, reduce reliance on one-time equipment sales, and strengthen the model as utilization expands.

More than 80 sites are already onboarded to EnergyConnect, including 52 U.S. owned DC fast-charging sites, and demand fees fell 21% across nine sites. This operating capability can improve site economics and create a scalable energy-management layer around Blink’s charging network.

bear.b: Revenue weakness remains a fundamental growth concern: Q3 revenue fell year over year and full-year guidance was cut to $78–81 million. Continued project timing pressure and portfolio rationalization could limit scale, making it harder for recurring services and infrastructure expansion to offset weaker product sales.

Despite improvement, Blink remains deeply unprofitable, with TTM EBIT and net margins near -55% and -63%, respectively, while free cash flow was about -$13.6 million. Persistent losses and cash burn constrain internal funding and leave execution dependent on continued financial resources.

Blink’s newer EnergyConnect and battery-storage opportunity is expected to remain relatively small in 2027, with growth only accelerating in the second half. That limits near-term diversification and means the company must still prove these initiatives can become material, profitable revenue streams.
